page_title: Effective context engineering for AI agents

sources.entry: Effective Context Engineering for AI Agents by Anthropic - Anthropic's guide to curating the context window — compaction, just-in-time retrieval, and note-taking — the discipline underlying effective long-horizon agent use.

summary.name: Effective context engineering for AI agents
summary.one_liner: An Anthropic engineering guide arguing that building capable LLM agents depends on curating the limited context window, covering compaction, structured note-taking, sub-agent architectures and just-in-time retrieval.
use_cases: Keeping a long-running coding agent coherent across hours of work
Deciding what to keep when summarizing an agent's conversation
Designing token-efficient tools for an AI agent
Letting an agent retrieve files or data on demand instead of preloading them
Giving an agent persistent notes or memory outside the context window
Structuring system prompts and few-shot examples for agents
summary.what_it_does: The page is an essay, not a software product, explaining context engineering as the successor to prompt engineering: curating every token that reaches a model during inference, including system prompts, tools, examples, message history and external data. It describes context rot, where recall degrades as the token count grows, and frames context as a finite attention budget. It recommends a minimal set of high-signal tokens, tools with little overlap, and a small set of diverse examples instead of long lists of edge-case rules. For long-horizon work it describes three techniques: compaction (summarizing a near-full context and restarting), structured note-taking written to external memory, and sub-agents that return condensed summaries. It also covers just-in-time retrieval using lightweight references, with Claude Code's CLAUDE.md and glob/grep used as examples of a hybrid approach.
notable: Defines context rot: recall accuracy falls as the context window fills, and this holds across models
Describes compaction, structured note-taking and multi-agent sub-agents as the three techniques for long-horizon tasks
Explains Claude Code's hybrid approach: CLAUDE.md loaded up front, with glob and grep for just-in-time file retrieval
caveats: Describes Anthropic's own products and approaches (Claude Code, Claude Developer Platform memory tool), so examples are vendor-specific
Runtime exploration is slower than pre-computed retrieval and needs careful tool and heuristic design
Advice is general guidance rather than measured benchmarks, and it says it will change as models improve
